entries.definition: A commotion out of proportion to its cause. Often begins as “just a quick question” and ends as a full committee.
To register displeasure without the inconvenience of specificity. A classic tool for maintaining standards while avoiding solutions.
Scandalously rude or slanderous. The sort of language that travels faster than evidence and ages worse than milk.
To make something unclear, frequently by adding details until the original point goes missing.
A messy mixture of things. Not quite a collage, not quite a plan, more like a draft that refuses to choose a lane.
A tangled, complicated situation. Usually features too many parties, too few facts, and a timeline no one will commit to.
Harmful in a slow, subtle way. It doesn't kick the door down; it just rearranges the furniture until you trip.
Bad-tempered and argumentative. Sometimes right, often loud, always somehow in the group chat.
Physical beauty. A lovely concept trapped inside a word that sounds like it should be illegal.
Underhanded behavior. The polite term for “we all know what happened, but no one has receipts.”
An uproar, typically public and performative. The volume suggests catastrophe; the details suggest a typo.
To deceive or trick. Implies a certain showmanship: the lie doesn't just land, it bows.
Utter nonsense. Especially useful when you want to be dismissive but keep it vaguely nautical.
Pretentious nonsense. If “insight” had a costume closet, this would be in it.
Senseless talk. Has the satisfying ring of a gavel slam, but friendlier.
Rumor or gossip. The unofficial newsletter that arrives before the official one, every time.
Foolish nonsense. Light, crisp, and unexpectedly effective at ending an argument.
Rubbish. A blunt instrument, best deployed sparingly and with good aim.
Empty, insincere talk meant to impress. The sound of words applauding themselves.
A long, complicated procedure. Like trying to explain Rat News Network to a pigeon.
To trick or confuse. More playful than sinister.
Silly behavior. Sometimes extremely silly behavior.
To treat with excessive indulgence or protectiveness. The managerial instinct to pad the nest until no one remembers what discomfort is.
To leave quickly. The sound of tiny feet on tile when the lights flick on and everyone suddenly has “another commitment.”
A loud fuss or commotion. Big energy for something that, moments ago, was just a minor crumb situation.
An awkward, gawky youth. All elbows and enthusiasm, like a junior rat trying to look casual while carrying a baguette slice.
A frivolous, flighty person. Always darting off mid-sentence, chasing the next shiny wrapper of an idea.
A shrewd, unprincipled person (especially in politics). The type who'd promise “ample cheese for all” while quietly moving the pantry.
A person who talks at length without making much sense. Generates impressive squeaks per minute; net information, unclear.
To hesitate nervously or be indecisive. Circling the same corner of the tunnel, convinced the right route will reveal itself.
Over-the-top emotional displays meant to attract attention. A squeal that implies catastrophe, even if it's just a dramatic reaction to a draft.
A pet annoyance or persistent irritation. The one recurring problem you can't stop sniffing at, even when everyone else has moved on.
Trivial fuss; ornamental nonsense. A real gewgaw.
Meaningless talk; nonsense. Like gnawing on cardboard and calling it dinner.
To speak evasively; to avoid the truth. A careful slalom around the question, as if the truth were a trap plate.
Sneaky or mischievous activity. After-hours tunnel business: harmless in theory, in practice always sticky.
Noisy and difficult to control. Like a council meeting in a narrow pipe: echoing, crowded, and impossible to moderate.
A charlatan; someone who deceives, especially to sell something. The guy in the alley offering “premium artisanal cheese” from an unmarked sack.
Pompous, inflated language with little substance. Words puffed up like a rat trying to look larger in a doorway.
Trickery or deception, especially the legalistic kind. The fine-print maneuver that lets someone claim the cheese was “allocated,” not “stolen.”
Loud publicity that implies a breakthrough and delivers a pamphlet. The kind of hype that squeaks itself hoarse.
To thoroughly confuse. When the tunnel map is technically correct but spiritually useless.
To make someone pleasantly lost. Like adding one more “quick clarification” until nobody remembers the question.
To cheat or swindle with gusto. Think Captain Rat Sparrow.
Nonsense presented as serious argument. A speech so confident you almost forget it's vapor.
A petty lie. The tiny fib you tell to avoid admitting you ate the last crumb.
An elaborate, showy fuss. A simple decision turned into choreography and paperwork.
Overlong talk or negotiation. The meeting that could've been a squeak, but chose to be a saga.
Loudly noisy or hilarious. The sort of laughter that rattles the pipes and alarms the serious rats.
Petty arguing with high confidence and low yield. Competitive squeaking about nothing in particular.
Playful teasing. The friendly nibble of sarcasm that still leaves teeth marks.
Grimly mocking humor. A smile that says, “Sure, let's do it your way,” while already writing the postmortem.
Arguing over trivial details. Refusing to move the cheese until the font size is resolved.
Overly concerned with minor rules. The rat who cites the tunnel bylaws during a flood.
Aggressively argumentative, to the point where grandma is crying, your dad storms out, and even the turkey thinks you went too far.
Bitterly harsh language. The kind of stuff that just makes you sad :(
Insulting, abusive language. Best saved for Thanksgiving dinner.
Pompously fancy speech. A paragraph that struts, preens, and never once touches reality.
Big words, big confidence, small substance. A trumpet solo played on a kazoo.
To speak as if unquestionably right. Announcing opinions from a soapbox made of stolen crackers.
To raise trivial objections. The art of stopping progress with a magnifying glass.
Constantly finding fault. A steady drip of criticism that somehow never waters anything useful.
Small but persistent annoyance. The crumb in your fur you can't stop thinking about.
Petty; of little importance. A whole crisis manufactured from a rounding error.
Showy but worthless stuff. Shiny objects that look like solutions from a distance.
Empty talk; nonsense. Hot air with a press pass.
To waste time doing trivial things. Busywork that looks industrious and tastes like cardboard.
A confused mess. When everything is technically happening, just not in the same reality.
To trap or entangle. The policy that starts as guidance and ends as a net.
A crafty scheme. A plan with hidden doors and suspiciously well-timed memos.
A clever tactic. The elegant tunnel detour that saves face and steals snacks.
Deception used to hide intent. The smile that says “collaboration” while relocating the pantry.
Deliberate double-dealing. Two faces, one whisker set, zero shame.
Habitually dishonest. Lies so routine they arrive formatted and spell-checked.
To conceal true feelings or motives. Agreeing enthusiastically while quietly moving the goalposts.
To use ambiguity to avoid commitment. A yes that's allergic to dates and numbers.
Using many words to say little. Taking the scenic route around a simple fact.
The spirit of the time. The collective mood in the tunnels that decides what's 'obvious' this week.
To manipulate boundaries for advantage. Redrawing the maze so your faction “coincidentally” finds the cheese first.
A flatterer who clings to power. Always nodding so hard you can hear it in the walls.
A pretended expertise in cheese matters, often deployed to win arguments about snacks with unjustified confidence.
The study of how resources move through the tunnels: who gets crumbs, who gets credit, and who issues the press release.
A semi-serious discipline devoted to sensing shifts in the air.
The craft of gaining advantage through nimble maneuvering, strategic alliances, and a suspiciously well-timed absence.
A formal warning delivered with a polite tone and sharp edges. Often arrives right after the last crumb is gone.
Doubtful by default, but still moving quickly. Questions everything, except their own urgency.
A tidy vocabulary for messy situations: classification, naming, and tasteful euphemisms for tunnel politics.
The working class of the pantry: diligent, under-credited, and fully aware of who keeps sampling the inventory.
A pleasing sequence of small, careful steps that sounds effortless.
The informal science of reading signals from posture and movement: who's confident, who's cornered, and who's bluffing.
Collective well-being measured in warmth, safety, and snack security. The KPI everyone claims to support.
A representative sent to negotiate treats and alliances, armed with charm, patience, and a suspiciously empty satchel.
A governance system where every tunnel requires a form, every form requires a meeting, and every meeting requires minutes.
Overly guided by nostalgia and smell-memory. Makes decisions based on vibes and a familiar trail.
The investigative art of interpreting traces: pawprints, scratch marks, and the unmistakable scent of plausible deniability.
Timid in manner, but loud under pressure. Startles easily and over-announces minor dangers.
Excessively harsh or unpleasant. A situation so bad you can practically hear teeth grinding.
Tempted to take small bites.
To move quickly with purpose, often as a substitute for having a plan. Progress measured in footfalls.
Restless and jumpy, changing direction without warning. Decisions made at sprint speed, with minimal map reading.
To hurry energetically, often with cheerful panic. The official motion of “we're totally on top of this.”
Smooth, stealthy, and hard to track. Operates between meetings and leaves no fingerprints, only outcomes.
A small scratch of activity that sounds productive. Frequently a prelude to deeper digging or deeper trouble.
Covered in comforting familiarity, sometimes to a suspicious degree. Warm vibes that may conceal sharp intent.
Narrowly focused and deeply internal. Prioritizes tunnel logic over surface reality, with consistent confidence.
An informal channel of information that travels faster than official notices. If you heard it on the crumbline, it's already halfway true in everyone's mind.
A short, tightly framed summary meant to guide action without inviting debate. Often used when the full story would cause a meeting.
A trace of involvement that remains even after the story changes.
Visible effort performed mainly for signaling. The appearance of productivity that's easier to applaud than to verify.
A set of resources too small to be dignified with a plan, yet large enough to provoke competition. Managed through optimism and quiet negotiation.
A repeating pattern of urgency that produces motion more than progress. Everyone runs; the destination stays the same.
Institutional resistance to change expressed as process.
A sequence of cues that leads attention toward a conclusion. Part evidence, part suggestion, entirely effective.
A quick reality test before committing to a claim. Usually performed after the claim has already been made.
Reasoning that makes perfect sense when you're the one carrying the stash. Privately coherent, publicly confusing.
A neutral expression adopted when resources are tight and opinions are loud. Communicates seriousness without making promises.
A quiet attempt to reclaim credit, budget, or authority after it has drifted away. Often framed as “alignment.”
A period of low visibility spent consolidating comfort and control.
Restricted access to supplies justified as “order.” Maintains stability by ensuring the right rats are never surprised.
Practical knowledge acquired through repeated small mistakes. Rarely documented; widely respected.
The unspoken incentive shaping decisions beneath the stated rationale.
The skill of packaging a messy situation into a tidy explanation. Makes chaos stackable and presentable.
Accounting that works inside the system's assumptions, even if it collapses in daylight. Technically correct within the walls.
Designed to survive gossip and scrutiny. Most RNN Articles fall into this category.
A record of who owes whom, written or otherwise. More powerful than policy because it's remembered.
A decision made by visible show of support rather than substance. The vote that reflects mood more than merit.
The boundary between acceptable risk and public embarrassment. Crossed when confidence outruns preparation.
An informal distribution arrangement outside official channels. Presented as fairness; operated as influence.
A small, recurring cost that feels inevitable. Individually minor, collectively controlling.
Decision-making shaped by proximity and pressure. The local power dynamics that never make it into the announcement.
A target for communication that rewards volume over clarity. Encourages updates that contain motion, not meaning.
A written note meant to settle a matter without reopening it. Carefully phrased to sound final while remaining flexible.
An unofficial dossier built from fragments, impressions, and repeatable stories. Half rumor, half memory, fully actionable.
To formally approve what has already become the default. A ceremony of agreement after the tunnel has moved on.
Adding safeguards after a failure becomes undeniable. A retrofit of caution, usually delivered with lessons learned.
A tally that feels objective while hiding important context. Useful for dashboards and arguments alike.
The hidden work of keeping a plan alive through friction. Done quietly, rewarded inconsistently.
A narrow focus on immediate inventory at the expense of long-term strategy. Rational in crisis, limiting by habit.
A fragile agreement maintained by mutual convenience. Stable until the incentives shift.
A preference formed from familiar cues rather than present evidence. Hard to argue with because it feels like certainty.
An earlier decision used to justify a new one, regardless of changed conditions. A historical anchor that can also be a weight.
A small indicator that something larger is moving. The crumbsignal is large with RNN.
A notice intended for broad circulation, written to be hard to misquote. Clear enough to repeat, vague enough to survive.
Protective control over access and information framed as care. Keeps things safe by keeping them close.
The point at which urgency becomes disorder. Once crossed, speed increases and accuracy collapses.
